outcome_variable_scope: The drop rebuilt here is judge-relative and gold-relative: the ranking target is the r08 model gold head, not human rankings (entry 50, r47). Reliability along any axis is not validity.
scope: Split-half over a prompt's criteria, 2-2, Spearman-Brown corrected, averaged over 200 random splits with the spread reported -- a single split moved the drop's reliability from 0.3013 to 0.3911. Prompts with K<4 are excluded and counted. The full-criteria rebuild reproduces the persisted accuracies exactly. The three floors-by-world columns are ARITHMETIC UNDER AN ASSUMPTION, not three measurements: only the published column corresponds to a decision this repository has made. Which world is right is a question about what the measurement program holds fixed, and is left open deliberately.
verdict: THE LEDGER'S FLOOR FORMULA MULTIPLIES TWO RELIABILITIES ESTIMATED ALONG DIFFERENT AXES, and nobody wrote that down, including me in r67 and r69. r57 measured the outcome by splitting the 6 PAIRS -- the response axis. r67 and r69 measured predictors by splitting CRITERIA. Rebuilding the attribution drop from half a prompt's criteria, on a tensor whose full-criteria rebuild reproduces r12's published per-prompt values exactly, the outcome's criterion-axis reliability is 0.3013 -- close to r57's 0.302/0.422, so the two axes agree for the OUTCOME even though they differ roughly twofold for r54's predictor. THE LADDER IS THE FINDING: accuracy 0.6462, attribution 0.2695, drop 0.3013. The criterion split does not destroy signal by itself, so the loss belongs to the contrast, and r57's own untested worry is confirmed: a difference of two accuracies is far less reliable than either. A SINGLE SPLIT IS NOT A MEASUREMENT: this round's first version drew one and got 0.3911 for the drop; over 200 splits the mean is 0.3013, with the raw correlation ranging +0.0922 to +0.3225. r57 averaged 200 splits; r69 drew one, and is corrected alongside this round. MAY THE AXES BE MULTIPLIED -- testable, unlike the choice of world: crossed +0.0785 [+0.0061,+0.1480] against +0.0463 if independent and +0.1808 if one shared source. INDEPENDENT -- world B may multiply the two axes. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: whether a floor is ENTITLED to divide by criterion-axis reliability at all. Under F, R is part of M(R,J,pi,Q,P) and this rubric's criteria are not error, so the 1.23x is an over-correction. Under S the current floors stand. Under B the rows are mechanism claims, both axes are error, and r54's floor would be 0.669 rather than 0.367. NO WINNER IS DECLARED HERE, because that is a decision about the research object and this round measured a correlation.
